The platform never reads the bag — it is not an IAM context, not a policy input and not part of a prompt — which is what separates it from a tag bag.

policy_ids.description: The policies every run of the eval acts under. Empty for one written without any, which does not run until a write gives it one.

group_by.description: The item `metadata` key a run rolls its scores up by; null when the eval groups nothing

Scorers.description:
Scorer configs, a discriminated union on `type`. Each type may appear at most once. Every scorer produces `{ score: 0–1, passed: boolean }`; binary scorers emit 0 or 1.

`exact_match` compares the trimmed output text to `expected_output`. `contains` looks for `value` in the output text. `json_logic` evaluates `expression` over `{ input, output, object, expected, item.metadata }`, where `object` is the structured output (absent when the agent has no `output_schema`). `output_schema` validates the structured output against the scorer's own `schema`, falling back to the agent's; it requires the agent to carry an `output_schema`, because without one the platform emits no structured output and every item would score 0.

`llm_judge` grades the output with a model completion, returning a continuous score plus its `reasoning`. Its `pass_threshold` is required: a continuous score says nothing about where "good enough" is, and a defaulted cutoff would silently decide the gate.

`embedding_similarity` embeds the output text and `expected_output` with the platform's configured embedding model (`EMBEDDING_PROVIDER` / `EMBEDDING_MODEL` — the same stack document ingestion uses) and scores their cosine similarity, clamped to 0-1. Its `pass_threshold` is required for the same reason as the judge's. An item without an `expected_output` scores 0; an embedding backend failure marks the **item** errored, never a score of 0.

`tool` runs a custom scoring algorithm: a server-callable project tool the engine invokes once per item with the item's context. Unlike the built-in types it may appear several times, each under a distinct `name` — outcomes and aggregates key on the name.

`decider` grades each item with a decision of a project decider: its `score` expression reads the decision's `answers`. Like `tool`, it keys on its `name` and may appear several times.

expression.description: A JSON Logic expression; a truthy result scores 1

schema.description: JSON Schema the structured output is validated against. Frozen here so two runs stay comparable; falls back to the agent's `output_schema` when omitted.

pass_threshold.description: The item passes this scorer when the cosine similarity between the embeddings of the output text and `expected_output` is greater than or equal to this value. Required.

prompt.description: The judge prompt. `{{input}}`, `{{output}}` and `{{expected}}` are replaced with the item's input messages, the agent's output text, and the item's `expected_output`. Slots are filled in one pass, so a slot value that itself contains `{{output}}` is not re-expanded. The judge must answer with a JSON object carrying a numeric `score` between 0 and 1 and an optional `reasoning` string; a reply that does not marks the **item** errored, never the run failed and never a score of 0.
prompt.example: Rate 0-1 how well the answer matches the reference. Answer with {"score": <0-1>, "reasoning": "<why>"}. Question: {{input}} Answer: {{output}} Reference: {{expected}}

pass_threshold.description: The item passes this scorer when the judge's score is greater than or equal to this value. Required.

ai_provider_id.description: The AI provider that runs the judge; it must belong to the eval's project. Omit to use the project's default model route.

model.description: Overrides the provider's default model. Pinned per scorer, because deltas between runs judged by different models are not comparable.

ToolScorer.description: A custom scoring algorithm — a server-callable project tool the engine invokes once per item. The tool receives the same variables a `json_logic` expression reads — `input`, `output`, `object` (when the agent has an `output_schema`), `expected`, and `item.metadata` — with `preset_parameters` merged in at the top level, and must answer with a JSON object carrying a numeric `score` between 0 and 1, an optional boolean `passed`, and an optional `reasoning` string. A malformed answer or a failed call marks the **item** errored, never the run failed and never a score of 0.

name.description: Keys this scorer's outcomes and aggregate scores, so it must be unique within the eval and must not shadow a built-in scorer type. Unlike the built-in types, several `tool` scorers may coexist under distinct names.

tool_id.description: The tool that scores each item. It must belong to the eval's project and be server-callable (`http`, `mcp`, `builtin`, or `pipeline` — a `client` tool pauses for a calling client an eval run does not have).

action.description: The operation to invoke; required when the tool type is `builtin` or `mcp`.

preset_parameters.description: Fixed values merged into every call's input at the top level. The engine-injected keys (`input`, `output`, `object`, `expected`, `item`) are reserved and rejected.

pass_threshold.description: Fallback verdict cutoff when the tool answers without a `passed` flag: the item passes this scorer when `score` is greater than or equal to this value. A tool-returned `passed` always wins. When the tool omits `passed` and no threshold is set, the item is recorded as errored — the scorer produced no verdict.

DeciderScorer.description: Grades each item with a decision of a project decider, under the decider version pinned when the run started (`decider_versions` on the run). The decision is requested as the run, with `metadata` naming the eval, run and dataset item. A failed decision, or a `score` that is not a number between 0 and 1, marks the **item** errored, never a score of 0.

name.description: Keys this scorer's outcomes and aggregate scores, so it must be unique within the eval and must not shadow a built-in scorer type.

decider_id.description: The decider that judges each item; it must belong to the eval's project.

input.description: JSON Logic mapping over `{ input, output, object, expected, item }` building the input the decider judges. Omitted, the input is that item context itself.

score.description: JSON Logic expression over `{ answers, answers_by_name }`, the decision's answers in question order and keyed by question name, that evaluates to the item's score in 0–1.

pass_threshold.description: The item passes this scorer when `score` is greater than or equal to this value. Required: a score read from a distribution says nothing about where "good enough" is.

AttachedPolicyIds.description: The policies the resource acts under; an event subscriber receives an event only when they allow reading its resource. The caller must hold every grant of each one it attaches inside the project, else `403 POLICY_GRANT_NOT_HELD`.

agent_id.description: The agent every item of this run executed against, resolved when the run was created and kept after that agent is deleted or the eval is pointed at another. Null for a run that recorded none, which satisfies no promotion gate.

agent_version.description: The one agent version every item in this run executed against

decider_versions.description: The decider version each `decider` scorer grades under, keyed by scorer name and resolved when the run started. Null when the eval has no decider scorer.

trigger_id.description: The trigger that started this run — set when a schedule (or a manual trigger fire) started it, null for a run started through this API. Kept even if the trigger is later deleted.

passed.description: Null when the eval declares no pass_threshold, and until the run is terminal

metadata.description: The caller-owned key/value metadata supplied when the run was started, returned verbatim. Absent when the run was started without any (a trigger-started run included — see `trigger_id` for that provenance). The server writes nothing here.

EvalRunDefinition.description: The eval's scorers, pass threshold and grouping key as they were when the run was created. Every item is scored and the run settled by these; a later edit to the eval reaches only runs created after it. Null when the run recorded none.

pass_threshold.description: Null when the run reports without gating

AggregateScores.description: Per-scorer rollup plus the run-level pass rate; null until the run is terminal

pass_rate.description: Passed items over non-errored items; null when nothing was scorable

scored_item_count.description: Items that produced a score — errored items are excluded

PassRateInterval.description: 95% Wilson score interval around `pass_rate`: the range the pass rate of this agent over items like these plausibly spans, given how many items were scored. Null exactly when `pass_rate` is.

BaselineComparison.description:
Comparison against the run named by `baseline_run_id`; absent when the run named none.

Every number here is computed over the **item intersection** — the dataset items present and scorable in both runs — because a delta only means something when both sides answered the same question. The compared/added/removed counts make any dataset drift visible instead of letting it read as agent regression. Positive deltas mean this run scored higher than the baseline.

compared_item_count.description: Items scorable in both runs — the basis of every delta

added_item_count.description: Scorable here but not in the baseline (added, or errored there)

removed_item_count.description: Scorable in the baseline but not here (removed, or errored here)

pass_rate_delta.description: Run-level pass-rate delta over the intersection; null when the two runs share no comparable item

p_value.description: Exact McNemar p-value of the `flipped` split: the probability of a split at least this uneven were an item equally likely to flip either way, which is what an unchanged agent produces. `1` when no item flipped; null when the runs share no comparable item.

scorers.description: Per-scorer deltas, keyed by scorer type. A scorer only one of the two runs ran is omitted rather than compared against nothing.

FlippedItems.description: Compared items that changed verdict. `pass_rate_delta` is `(improved - regressed) / compared_item_count`.

improved.description: Passed in this run, failed in the baseline

regressed.description: Failed in this run, passed in the baseline

BaselineGrouping.description: The baseline comparison per group; absent when the eval declares no `group_by`. Both runs' items are grouped by the same labels, so an item relabelled between the runs is compared within one group.

ungrouped_item_count.description: Items scorable in both runs that name no group

GroupComparison.description: One group's baseline comparison, computed as the run-level one is

RunGrouping.description: Scores rolled up per value of the eval's `group_by` key; absent when the eval declares none. An item belongs to the group its `metadata` names under that key, read when the run settles; only a string names a group. Errored items count in no group.

group_by.description: The metadata key the groups were read from

ungrouped_item_count.description: Scored items whose `metadata` holds no string under `group_by`, or whose dataset item was deleted

ScoreRollup.description: One group's figures, computed as the run-level ones are

pass_rate.description: Passed items over non-errored items in the group

dataset_item_id.description: Null once the dataset item has been deleted

output.description: The agent's final output text. Cleared when the linked generation's content is purged; the scores and the frozen input survive.

passed.description: AND over the per-scorer passed flags

error.description: Item-level failure reason. A generation that did not complete — a `requires_action` pause (`GENERATION_NOT_COMPLETED`), a provider failure — or a scorer that could not grade the output is recorded here and excluded from the aggregates rather than scored 0.

scorer.description: The scorer that produced this entry — the scorer type, or for a `tool` scorer its `name`

reasoning.description: The stated rationale; present for `llm_judge` and for `tool` scorers whose tool returned one

decision_id.description: The decision that graded this entry; present for `decider` scorers

StoredError.description: Why a resource's work failed, in the shape of an error response's `error` without `hint` and `docs_url`. Every `error` field a resource records carries it, so `code` can be read without first checking the type of `error`.

code.description: A key from the server's ERROR_CODES registry, documented on the Error Codes page. `INTERNAL_ERROR`, with the message `Internal Server Error`, records an unexpected failure whose detail reaches the server log only.

meta.description: The failure's own structured context, when it names any.

version_label.description: Optional tag for the config version this write creates (e.g. `initial`). Annotates the version only — it is not stored on the guardrail and is not part of the config, so labelling a change is never itself a change.

GuardrailDocument.description: The action-class document. `class` maps a call to an action class; `guard` gates class-B autonomy. Both are single JSON Logic expressions over the `args.*` / `context.*` / `runtime.*` namespaces.

class.description: A class literal (`A` / `B` / `C` / `D`) or a JSON Logic expression returning one. An invalid result resolves to `default_class`.

default_class.description: Applied when the `class` expression returns anything other than a valid class. Defaults to `C` (fail-closed).

guard.description: A single JSON Logic expression; when the call classifies as `B` it must evaluate truthy to execute autonomously. Compose multiple conditions with `{ "and": [...] }`.

escalate.description: When `true`, a failing guard routes to approval instead of tripping fail-closed.

expires_in.description: Default approval window in seconds for a class-C approval this guardrail files. Omitted → the platform's 24h default. When several guardrails apply, the governing (strictest-matching) one's value is used.

project_id.description: Public ID of the owning project

version.description: Incremented on every document write; prior versions are archived

context_tool_id.description: Optional tool the platform calls at evaluation time to fetch fresh guardrail context.

context_mode.description: How tool-fetched context combines with the caller-supplied context.

version_label.description: Optional tag for the config version this write creates (e.g. `tightened`). Annotates the version only — it is not stored on the guardrail and is not part of the config, so labelling a change is never itself a change. Ignored when the write changes no policy, since no version is created.

expected_version.description: Refuses the write unless the resource is at this version.

GuardrailVersion.description: An immutable archive of a guardrail's configuration at one version.

id.description: Public ID of the archived version

guardrail_id.description: Public ID of the guardrail this version belongs to

config.description:
The guardrail's versioned surface as it stood at this version. Today that is the policy `document` and nothing else: name, description and the context binding are metadata, and bumping the version when one of them changes would make two version numbers denote the same policy — which is exactly what an evaluation record cites.

Deliberately open rather than a fixed schema: an archive written by an earlier release of SOAT reflects the guardrail surface **of its own time**, so it may carry fields the current API no longer documents.

label.description: Optional human tag for this version, e.g. `tightened`. Set from the `label` field of a restore, or generated for one.

created_by_principal_type.description: Who produced this version. Null for a write with no principal behind it.

created_by_principal_id.description: Public id of that principal: the user (`user_…`), or for API key auth the key itself (`key_…`), so the record names which key acted.

PrincipalType.description: What kind of principal acted. `user` and `api_key` are authenticated callers, and the id is the user's (`user_…`) or the key's own (`key_…`), so a record names which key acted rather than its owner. `agent` is an agent writing under its own identity (`agent_…`). `automation` is the task engine acting on a dispatch outcome and `approval` an approval resolution; neither carries an id. `trigger` is a trigger firing under its own `policy_ids` (`trg_…`). `system` is the platform itself, with an id naming the mechanism (`retention_sweep`, `zero_retention`). `eval`, `decider`, `ingestion_rule`, `memory_rule` and `playbook_version` are that resource's work running under its own `policy_ids` when nobody started it, the id its own.

label.description: Optional tag for the version the restore creates. Defaults to `restored from v<version>`.

GuardrailEvaluation.description: The record produced by evaluating a guardrail against one call — written to the audit trail at dispatch time (one per applying guardrail) and returned verbatim by the dry-run endpoint.

guardrail_version.description: The governing version; null for a dangling reference (fail-closed C).

class.description: The resolved class (or the applied default_class).

guard_result.description: The guard outcome; null when the call did not classify as B.

context_snapshot.description: Flat map of only the vars the class/guard expressions referenced, keyed by fully-qualified path, frozen at evaluation-time values.

ai_provider_id.description: AI provider in the route's project

model.description: Model name to call on that provider

timeout_seconds.description: Per-attempt deadline, enforced with an AbortSignal composed with the caller's signal. A timeout classifies as `timeout`; the caller's own signal firing aborts the run without failover. Omitted means no per-target deadline.

max_retries.description: Retries on this target before falling through to the next one. The route is the only retry authority — routed calls pass `maxRetries: 0` to the AI SDK so its own retry loop cannot multiply these.

project_id.description: The project the policy belongs to; `null` for a global policy.

condition.description: Optional condition block. Keys are condition operators (e.g. StringEquals) mapping to context-key/value maps; evaluated by the policy compiler. A context key must be one the platform supplies — `iam:ResourceType` or `iam:ResourceTag/<tag>` — because an unknown key is absent from the evaluation context, so a `Deny` naming one would never deny. The tag name after the slash is opaque and unconstrained. Operator and context keys are matched by exact string and are never case-converted, so they round-trip exactly as written: `iam:ResourceTag/cost_center` selects the tag `cost_center`, not `costCenter`.

guardrail_ids.description: Guardrails attached at the project scope — the baseline governing every tool call by every agent in the project.

agent_policy_ids.description: Policies capping every turn of every agent the project owns, on every path the agent's own `policy_ids` cap and on its stored `knowledge_config` retrieval. `null` adds no cap.

content_bound_tag_keys.description: Tag keys that state a judgment about what an agent can read, such as a screening verdict. A write that changes a document's content, title, path or metadata, re-ingests it, or changes a memory's content or metadata, removes these keys from its tags unless the same write sets them; a superseding memory does not inherit them. Empty when the project names none.

max_concurrent_runs.description: Maximum orchestration runs of this project driven at once. `null` means unlimited (the default). Enforced at queue claim time.

max_chain_generations.description: Generations one continuation chain in this project may hold before the platform stops resuming it. `null` means no project ceiling (the default), leaving the deployment-wide one. The effective budget is the smallest of the deployment's ceiling, this one, and the agent's own `max_chain_generations` stop condition.

max_orchestration_run_depth.description: `loop` / `sub_orchestration` nesting levels a run tree in this project may reach before the engine refuses to start the next child. `null` means no project bound (the default), leaving the deployment-wide one. The effective bound is the smaller of the two.

default_model_route_id.description: Model route inherited by consumers in this project that bind neither `model_route_id` nor `ai_provider_id`. `null` means no default, so every consumer must bind explicitly.

audit_reads_enabled.description: Whether `GET` requests naming this project are recorded in the audit log. `false` by default — v1 audits mutations only.

require_priced_model.description: Whether a generation whose model carries no price row is refused with `409 MODEL_NOT_PRICED`. `false` by default, where an unpriced model runs and meters at `cost_usd: null`.

default_conversation_retrieval.description: What a conversation that names no `retrieval` of its own does. `none` by default.

trace_content_retention_days.description: Days of trace/generation content retention before the daily sweep purges it. `null` means retention is disabled (the default) and content is kept until purged on demand.

trace_content_mode.description: Whether trace/generation content is persisted. `full` by default; `none` is zero-retention — content is never written for any agent in this project.

paused_at.description: When the project was paused. `null` while it runs. While set, nothing new starts in the project — see pause-project.

pause_reason.description: The reason the pause was requested with, echoed as `pause_reason` on every run and task the pause parked. `null` while the project runs, or when the pause named none.

reason.description: Why the project is paused. Stored as `pause_reason` and carried onto every run and task the pause parks.
reason.example: anomaly detected by the spend monitor

id.description: Public ID of the price row

project_id.description: The project this price is scoped to

ai_provider_id.description: Always null for a project + provider-slug price

meter_type.description: `llm_tokens` for a token row or an agent's resource row, `tool_execution` for a tool's

resource.description: The tool or agent SRN a resource row prices; null for a SKU row

quantity.description: A resource row's quantity expression; null prices one per call

component.description: The token component this row prices (`input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cached_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`)

unit_price.description: USD per token for this component

effective_from.description: The row with the latest effective_from <= now() prices a call

meter_type.description: `llm_tokens` for a token row naming `provider` and `model`, or for an agent's resource row; `tool_execution` for a tool's resource row.

resource.description: The SRN of one tool or agent, `srn:<project_id>:<tool|agent>:<id>`, for a resource row; omit `provider` and `model`. A tool's row prices its `tool_execution` events, beside `tool_call`; an agent's prices its `llm_tokens` events, beside the provider cost. A client tool has no execution of its own and cannot be priced.

quantity.description: On a resource row only: JSON Logic giving the quantity `unit_price` multiplies, over `{ input, action, response, outcome, duration_ms }` for a tool and `{ response: { usage, cost_usd, steps, tool_calls, stop_reason }, outcome }` for an agent. Omit to price one per call. A result that is not a finite number >= 0 records quantity `0` and no cost.

provider.description: The provider slug of a token row

model.description: The model of a token row

component.description: The component this row prices: a token component (`input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cached_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`), or a resource row's own (`page`)

unit.description: `token` for token pricing; the resource component's unit otherwise

effective_from.description: Must be in the future; past prices are immutable

BadRequest.description: Invalid request — a query parameter or body field the operation does not declare, or a value that fails validation

TooManyRequests.description: `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` — a `requests` quota on the calling API key or its project is spent for the window; `Retry-After` says when it reopens

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the quota window admits a request again

InternalError.description: Unexpected server error — `INTERNAL_ERROR`, with the raw message never forwarded

PayloadTooLarge.description: `REQUEST_REJECTED` — the request body is over the size the body parser accepts

AdmissionUnavailable.description: The deployment's admission service is asked about this write and did not answer — `ADMISSION_UNAVAILABLE`; the write did not happen

VersionConflict.description: The resource has moved past the version this write read (`VERSION_CONFLICT`): a stated `expected_version` or `If-Match` no longer matches, or a concurrent write took the version first. `meta.current_version` names the version in force. Nothing is written.
